newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stock index rises to close above 2,100.
newsitem.headline: French stock index rises to close above 2,100.

text.p: French stocks rose more than one percent on Wednesday, lifting the CAC-40 index to a close above the 2,100 level, on investor relief that the U.S. Federal Reserve did not raise its interest rates.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 21.91 points, or 1.05 percent, at 2,103.41, helped by rising bond markets. The CAC-40 September futures contract rose 14 points to 2,100.
Volume was a heavy 6.3 billion francs.
* Shares in luxury goods group LVMH fell against the trend, closing down 2.82 percent at 1,101 francs, ahead of the group's results due on Thursday morning.

Analysts have downgraded their forecasts and now expect the group to report a first-half profit, excluding exceptionals, between 1.50 billion and 1.60 billion francs, compared with 1.46 billion francs last year.
* Promodes shares rose 3.86 percent to 1,372 francs as investors applauded its move to acquire control of Italy's hyper and supermarkets concern Gruppo G.
"The market is reacting positively to this news -- to any news of expansion abroad -- because French retailers can only expand now if they expand abroad," one trader said.

* Insurer Axa jumped 3.85 percent to 297 francs after the company reported a jump in net attributable profit to 1.98 billion francs from 1.30 billion for the first half. "The results were significantly better than expected," a trader said.
"Axa is the best insurance stock in the market," said another trader. Chairman Claude Bebear told a news conference Axa had no intention of selling its treasury stock.
* Insurer AGF rose 3.70 francs to 143.50 after Morgan Stanley raised its rating to outperform from neutral.
* Credit National finished down 30.90 francs at 278.40, a year low, after reporting a first-half loss.

It reported a net attributable loss of 112 million francs after restructuring charges linked to the takeover of BFCE. Brokers said the market was particularly disappointed by the 4.93 percent drop in net banking income to 1.98 billion francs. Societe Generale cut its rating to neutral from outperform.
* Pen and lighter group BIC fell 22 francs to close at 690 after reporting a smaller-than-expected profit rise to 339 million francs in the first half from 310 million.
* Renault closed up 3.95 percent at 123.80 francs after the group announced it would cut prices in France by up to five percent on some models to recapture lost market share.
